t: Relationship Strength Estimator: a plain-language overview
title: Relationship Strength Estimator: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Relationship Strength Estimator does and why archives need it. A relationship strength estimator scores connections: is this link between two records strong or weak, and why? It weighs the evidence — how often they co-occur, how recent, how specific — and produces a score with the reasons attached. Strong links and weak links are never confused.
demo:
# Relationship Strength Estimator - runnable demo (JAH-ATK197-000001)
RANK = 1
SIG = False
RELS = [('Ann', 'Bob', 12, 0.9, 0.8, ['s1', 's2', 's3']), ('Ann', 'Cat', 2, 0.3, 0.4, ['s1']), ('Bob', 'Dan', 5, 0.6, 0.9, ['s2', 's4'])]  # (a, b, freq, recency_0_1, specificity_0_1, sources)
W = {"freq": 0.3, "recency": 0.2, "specificity": 0.3, "corroboration": 0.2}
def score(r):
    a, b, freq, rec, spec, srcs = r
    f = min(1.0, freq/10.0)
    c = min(1.0, len(set(srcs))/3.0)
    s = W["freq"]*f + W["recency"]*rec + W["specificity"]*spec + W["corroboration"]*c
    band = "strong" if s >= 0.7 else "moderate" if s >= 0.45 else "weak" if s >= 0.25 else "tenuous"
    return round(s, 3), band
for r in RELS:
    s, band = score(r)
    print("[%-8s %.3f] %s <-> %s" % (band.upper(), s, r[0], r[1]))
    if RANK >= 2: print("    freq=%d recency=%.2f specificity=%.2f sources=%d" % (r[2], r[3], r[4], len(set(r[5]))))
if RANK >= 3:
    print("relationships scored:", len(RELS))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-STR-" + "JAH-ATK197-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK197-000001", "OK")

t: How the Relationship Strength Estimator works: the deep tour
title: How the Relationship Strength Estimator works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Relationship Strength Estimator does and why archives need it. Real estimators score relationships on explicit criteria: co-occurrence frequency, recency, specificity (a rare shared attribute beats a common one), source reliability, and corroboration count. Weights combine the criteria into a 0–1 score mapped to strength bands (strong, moderate, weak, tenuous), and every score carries its criterion breakdown. Thresholds are tuned on labeled relationship corpora, and the estimator reports which criterion dominated each verdict. Advanced systems calibrate scores so bands mean the same thing across relationship types, detect score inflation from duplicated sources (ten copies of one article are one piece of evidence), and track strength over time as new evidence arrives. Quality is measured by ranking agreement with expert judgments. The limits are genuinely unknowable relationships and adversarial evidence planting — the estimator discounts dependent sources and flags anomalous evidence spikes rather than scoring them at face value.

title: Using the Relationship Strength Estimator every day
description: Production: how the Relationship Strength Estimator runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. A relationship strength estimator scores connections: is this link between two records strong or weak, and why? It weighs the evidence — how often they co-occur, how recent, how specific — and produces a score with the reasons attached. Strong links and weak links are never confused.
demo:
# Relationship Strength Estimator - runnable demo (JAH-ATK197-000013)
RANK = 1
SIG = False
RELS = [('Ann', 'Bob', 12, 0.9, 0.8, ['s1', 's2', 's3']), ('Ann', 'Cat', 2, 0.3, 0.4, ['s1']), ('Bob', 'Dan', 5, 0.6, 0.9, ['s2', 's4'])]  # (a, b, freq, recency_0_1, specificity_0_1, sources)
W = {"freq": 0.3, "recency": 0.2, "specificity": 0.3, "corroboration": 0.2}
def score(r):
    a, b, freq, rec, spec, srcs = r
    f = min(1.0, freq/10.0)
    c = min(1.0, len(set(srcs))/3.0)
    s = W["freq"]*f + W["recency"]*rec + W["specificity"]*spec + W["corroboration"]*c
    band = "strong" if s >= 0.7 else "moderate" if s >= 0.45 else "weak" if s >= 0.25 else "tenuous"
    return round(s, 3), band
for r in RELS:
    s, band = score(r)
    print("[%-8s %.3f] %s <-> %s" % (band.upper(), s, r[0], r[1]))
    if RANK >= 2: print("    freq=%d recency=%.2f specificity=%.2f sources=%d" % (r[2], r[3], r[4], len(set(r[5]))))
if RANK >= 3:
    print("relationships scored:", len(RELS))

title: The Relationship Strength Estimator at archive scale
description: Production: how the Relationship Strength Estimator runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real estimators score relationships on explicit criteria: co-occurrence frequency, recency, specificity (a rare shared attribute beats a common one), source reliability, and corroboration count. Weights combine the criteria into a 0–1 score mapped to strength bands (strong, moderate, weak, tenuous), and every score carries its criterion breakdown. Thresholds are tuned on labeled relationship corpora, and the estimator reports which criterion dominated each verdict. Advanced systems calibrate scores so bands mean the same thing across relationship types, detect score inflation from duplicated sources (ten copies of one article are one piece of evidence), and track strength over time as new evidence arrives. Quality is measured by ranking agreement with expert judgments. The limits are genuinely unknowable relationships and adversarial evidence planting — the estimator discounts dependent sources and flags anomalous evidence spikes rather than scoring them at face value.
